questions.title: Earliest Finishing Task
questions.description:
Activity selection always begins with the task that frees its resource earliest. Spotting that task — the one with the smallest finish time — is the greedy first pick. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int earliestFinish(int[] start, int[] end)

It must return the START time of the activity with the smallest end time. All end times are distinct.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start times. Line 3: n end times.

Output Format:
One line with the start time of the earliest-finishing activity.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= start, end <= 1000, end[i] < end[j] for i != j (all end times distinct)
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= start, end <= 1000, end[i] < end[j] for i != j (all end times distinct)

questions.title: Shop Change Maker
questions.description:
A shop till gives change for a purchase using unlimited coins of the canonical denominations {1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 1000}. For this canonical system the greedy choice — always hand back the biggest coin that fits — yields the minimum coin count. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minCoinCount(int amount)

It must return the minimum number of coins totalling exactly amount (you may hardcode the denominations).

Input Format:
Line 1: the amount.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of coins.

Constraints:
1 <= amount <= 100000

questions.title: Grab the Biggest First
questions.description:
A greedy algorithm's very first move is usually to grab the most valuable item available. Scanning for the maximum is that reflex in its purest form. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int largestPick(int[] values)

It must return the largest value in the array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated values.

Output Format:
One line with the largest value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Two Smallest Together
questions.description:
When every pairing costs the same, the greedy exchange argument says: take the two cheapest items and put them together first. The drill is to find that cheapest pair. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int twoSmallestSum(int[] values)

It must return the sum of the two smallest values in the array (n >= 2).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated values.

Output Format:
One line with the sum of the two smallest values.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 50, 0 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Largest Coin That Fits
questions.description:
A greedy cashier always reaches for the biggest denomination that does not exceed the amount still owed — that is the first step of canonical coin change. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int largestCoin(int amount)

The canonical denominations are {1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 1000}. It must return the largest denomination that is <= amount.

Input Format:
Line 1: the amount.

Output Format:
One line with the largest fitting denomination.

Constraints:
1 <= amount <= 10000

questions.title: Finish Times in Order
questions.description:
Sorting the activities by finish time is the canonical first step of interval scheduling: afterwards a single left-to-right sweep can pack in the maximum set. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] sortedFinishTimes(int[] end)

It must return the finish times in ascending order (the harness prints them space-separated).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n finish times.

Output Format:
One line with the finish times in ascending order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= end <= 1000

questions.title: Meeting Clash Count
questions.description:
Two meetings clash when they occupy the same stretch of the calendar: start[i] < end[j] and start[j] < end[i]. Back-to-back meetings (one ends exactly when the next starts) do NOT clash. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int clashCount(int[] start, int[] end)

It must return how many pairs (i < j) of meetings clash.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start times. Line 3: n end times.

Output Format:
One line with the number of clashing pairs.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= start, end <= 1000

questions.title: One Conference Room
questions.description:
The office owns a single conference room. A batch of meeting requests fits into it only when no two meetings clash — one may start the instant another ends. A pairwise overlap test answers it. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String oneRoom(int[] start, int[] end)

It must return "YES" if all meetings can run in one room (no pair overlaps; touching is allowed), otherwise "NO".

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start times. Line 3: n end times.

Output Format:
One line, YES or NO.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= start, end <= 1000

questions.title: Top Discount Picks
questions.description:
A coupon drive lets a shopper stack the k biggest discount codes on one purchase — the obvious greedy choice is to sort and take the largest ones. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int topDiscountSum(int[] discounts, int k)

It must return the sum of the k largest discount values (1 <= k <= number of codes).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n discount values. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the sum of the k largest discounts.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= k <= n, 0 <= discounts <= 1000

questions.title: Cargo Van Loading
questions.description:
A delivery van has one capacity limit and the goal is to load as MANY orders as possible. The optimal greedy is to load the lightest orders first — an exchange argument shows no other choice fits more parcels. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int maxOrders(int[] weights, int cap)

It must return the maximum number of orders whose total weight fits in cap.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n order weights. Line 3: the van capacity cap.

Output Format:
One line with the number of orders loaded.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= weights <= 100, 1 <= cap <= 10000

questions.title: Limited Coin Register
questions.description:
A cash register holds exactly ONE coin of each canonical denomination {1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 1000}. Paying greedily, it hands out the biggest coin that still fits the remaining amount, each coin used at most once, until the amount is covered or no coin fits anymore. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int registerCoins(int amount)

It must return how many coins the register hands out under that greedy rule (even if the amount cannot be fully covered).

Input Format:
Line 1: the amount.

Output Format:
One line with the number of coins handed out.

Constraints:
1 <= amount <= 10000

questions.title: Lifeboat Patrol
questions.description:
A patrol boat carries at most TWO people per trip and never exceeds its weight limit. To minimise trips, pair the heaviest survivor with the lightest one who still fits — sort, then work inward with two pointers. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minBoats(int[] people, int limit)

It must return the minimum number of boat trips; every person's weight is <= limit, each boat takes one or two people whose summed weight is <= limit.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n people weights. Line 3: the boat weight limit.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of trips.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= people <= 1000, 1 <= limit <= 2000

questions.title: Cookie Distribution Drive
questions.description:
Volunteers hand out cookies: a child with greed factor g is content with any cookie of size >= g, and each cookie feeds at most one child. Sorting both lists and walking them with two pointers maximises the content children — the classic greedy assignment. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int assignCookies(int[] greed, int[] size)

It must return the maximum number of children that can be made content.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (children). Line 2: n greed factors. Line 3: m (cookies). Line 4: m cookie sizes.

Output Format:
One line with the number of content children.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 50, 0 <= greed, size <= 100

questions.title: Assignment Deadline Crunch
questions.description:
Every assignment takes exactly one time slot and must finish by its deadline. Sort the deadlines ascending and greedily fill slots 1, 2, 3, ... — take a job whenever its deadline is still ahead of the clock. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int maxJobs(int[] deadlines)

It must return the maximum number of assignments that can be completed.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n deadlines.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum number of assignments completed.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= deadlines <= 100

questions.title: Delivery Route Reach
questions.description:
A courier hops along delivery stops; nums[i] is the farthest next stop reachable from stop i. The greedy reach scan keeps the furthest index reachable so far — if the scan ever outruns it, the route is broken. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int canReachLast(int[] nums)

It must return 1 if the last stop is reachable from stop 0, otherwise 0. Stop 0 is the last stop when n == 1.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n jump distances.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= nums <= 100

questions.title: Channel Conflict Cleanup
questions.description:
Radio broadcasts overlap on the airwaves; a scheduler must DROP as few broadcasts as possible so the survivors never overlap (a broadcast may start exactly when another ends). Sorting by end time and keeping every broadcast that starts at or after the last kept end minimises removals. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minRemovals(int[] start, int[] end)

It must return the minimum number of broadcasts to remove so the rest are pairwise non-overlapping.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start times. Line 3: n end times.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of removals.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= start, end <= 1000

questions.title: Studio Session Scheduling
questions.description:
A recording studio receives many session requests; the manager wants to host as MANY sessions as possible. The classic greedy: sort sessions by finish time, then keep every session that starts at or after the last kept one ends (back-to-back is allowed). The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int maxActivities(int[] start, int[] end)

It must return the maximum number of non-overlapping sessions that can be scheduled.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start times. Line 3: n end times.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum number of sessions.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= start, end <= 10000

questions.title: Cargo Value Maximizer
questions.description:
A cargo drone has a weight limit and items can be SLICED: any fraction of an item may be taken, contributing proportional value. The fractional knapsack greedy sorts items by value/weight ratio and fills the drone with whole items, finally slicing the first item that does not fit. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static double fractionalKnapsack(int[] wt, int[] val, int cap)

It must return the maximum total value achievable (the harness prints the returned double with exactly 2 decimals).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n item weights. Line 3: n item values. Line 4: the capacity cap.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum value, printed with 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= wt, val <= 1000, 1 <= cap <= 10000

questions.title: Platform Headcount at Junction
questions.description:
A bus junction must shelter every coach: a coach occupies one platform from its arrival time until its departure time. The minimum number of platforms equals the maximum number of coaches present simultaneously. Sort arrivals and departures, then sweep with two pointers — no coach departs at the exact moment another arrives, so the comparison is unambiguous. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minPlatforms(int[] arrival, int[] departure)

It must return the minimum number of platforms needed.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n arrival times. Line 3: n departure times (departure[i] > arrival[i]; no departure equals any arrival).

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of platforms.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= arrival, departure <= 100000

questions.title: Balloon Burst Arrows
questions.description:
Balloons float along a horizontal axis; balloon i spans [start[i], end[i]]. One arrow shot vertically at position x bursts every balloon with start[i] <= x <= end[i]. Sorting balloons by end and shooting each arrow at the earliest-ending balloon's right edge minimises the arrow count. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minArrows(int[] start, int[] end)

It must return the minimum number of arrows needed to burst every balloon.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n start coordinates. Line 3: n end coordinates (end[i] >= start[i]).

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of arrows.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= start <= end <= 10000
